_notes: The languages a man can learn (systems/languages.ts): in seminary as an activity, in Rome as a study activity where offered, and as a priest through the study hours of the routine. Each is a credential, held for life; a community's Mass needs its language.

languages.label: Spanish
languages.line: You can hear confessions in Spanish now, slowly. The diocese will notice.

languages.label: Italian
languages.line: You can follow a lecture in Italian now, and argue with a porter.

languages.label: Latin
languages.line: You can read the Latin now, and say the older Mass without a card.

languages.label: French
languages.line: You can preach in French now, to the Haitians and the Africans and the one Québécois family, and read the older theology in it.

languages.label: German
languages.line: You can read Ratzinger in German now, and say Mass for the old families at Christmas.

languages.label: Polish
languages.line: You can say the Gorzkie żale now and hear a grandmother's confession in Polish, which she has waited twenty years for.

languages.label: Vietnamese
languages.line: The tones took a year and the community took a month to stop laughing kindly. You can say their Mass now.

languages.label: Tagalog
languages.line: You can preach in Tagalog now, badly and to applause, and the Santo Niño Mass is yours.

languages.label: Korean
languages.line: You can say the Korean Mass now and follow the catechists' meeting, most of it.
